sections.title: Commercial Mix & Delivery
sections.subtitle: Deal pipeline, client/industry diversification and the onsite-offshore delivery model -- disclosed quarterly since Q1 FY2026 except deal wins, which go back to Q2 FY2025

dealWins.title: Deal wins (TCV)
dealWins.content:
Total contract value (TCV) of new deals signed in the quarter, disclosed in US dollars -- the forward-revenue signal management highlights every result, since signed TCV converts to billed revenue over the following 12-24 months rather than immediately.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: TCV strengthened sharply through FY2026 (Q2 FY2025's $603m to over $1bn in Q3 and Q4 FY2026) alongside the turnaround plan management has been executing since the FY2024 margin reset.

What to watch:

  • TCV growth outpacing revenue growth (a leading indicator) versus falling behind it (bookings drying up)
  • Large-deal mix -- a few mega-deals can make one quarter's TCV lumpy
  • Conversion lag: a strong TCV quarter shows up in revenue two-plus quarters later

revenueMixGeo.title: Revenue mix by geography
revenueMixGeo.content:
Share of revenue from the Americas, Europe and Rest of World (which includes India and APAC).

For Tech Mahindra Limited: roughly half of revenue is Americas-dollar-denominated, so INR strength or weakness against the dollar moves reported rupee growth independently of underlying demand; Europe is the next-largest and most telecom-exposed region given the Communications vertical's European carrier base.

What to watch:

  • Americas share rising or falling relative to the diversification story management tells
  • Europe weakness tracking European telecom capex cycles

revenueMixVertical.title: Revenue mix by industry vertical
revenueMixVertical.content:
Share of revenue by the industry verticals Tech Mahindra reports: Communications (its largest and most distinctive vertical, built on telco network-services heritage), BFSI, Manufacturing, Technology & Media, Retail & Transport, Healthcare & Life Sciences and Others.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: Communications is roughly a third of revenue -- far more concentrated than peers Infosys or TCS -- which is why telecom carrier capex cycles (5G rollouts slowing, network spend cuts) hit this company harder than the sector average.

What to watch:

  • Communications share shrinking as management tries to diversify into BFSI and Manufacturing
  • Any single non-Communications vertical becoming large enough to offset telecom softness

clientConcentration.title: Client concentration
clientConcentration.content:
Share of revenue from the top 5, top 10 and top 20 clients -- the standard IT-services disclosure for customer-concentration risk.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: the top 5 clients run close to 15% of revenue and the top 20 near 38% -- losing or downsizing one top account (a known risk after past AT&T and Comcast-related volume cuts in Communications) moves the topline more than at a more fragmented peer.

What to watch:

  • Top-5/10/20 share widening (concentration rising) versus narrowing (new logo wins diluting it)
  • Concentration trend read alongside the Communications vertical mix above -- the two risks often share the same accounts

headcountMix.title: Headcount mix and offshore delivery
headcountMix.content:
Headcount split between IT services, BPS (business process services) and sales & support staff, plotted against the offshore mix -- the share of delivery effort performed from lower-cost offshore locations (mainly India) rather than onsite at the client.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: offshore mix near 78% is the main lever behind EBIT margin -- every point shifted offshore cuts delivery cost, and the FY2024-25 margin recovery plan leaned on this alongside the Tech Mahindra 4.0 structural cost actions (pyramid flattening, bench reduction).

What to watch:

  • Offshore mix stalling or reversing (client pushback, onsite-heavy new deals) pressuring margin
  • IT-services headcount shrinking faster than revenue (a utilization/automation story) versus client losses

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Tech Mahindra Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Tech Mahindra Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
